statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Overnight Nasdaq-100 conditions are orderly and range-bound, with elevated background stress from multi-year-high long-end yields and Gulf energy disruption.
recommendation: Conditions are consistent with a normal two-way regime. The published danger window covers 13:30-16:00 UTC, spanning the US cash open and the ISM Services release, where the mapped policy state is expected to move to WATCH.
headline: Quiet two-way overnight tape holds Tail low while yields near three-year highs keep Stress elevated
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are holding a narrow overnight band of roughly 70 points near 29,180 after the Sep 2 cash close at 29,143.33 (+0.23%, day range 28,971.90-29,165.62). The Nikkei is mid-range and modestly higher, VIX finished at 15.20 after a near 7% decline, and WTI is little changed near $91 with Brent near $95.50. No persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or session-extreme holding is observed, so Tail stays low. Stress remains elevated: the US 10-year yield reached 4.81% on Sep 2, the highest since late 2023, the 30-year is above 5.2%, and the Strait of Hormuz remains largely closed to commercial transits, keeping an inflation-through-energy channel open. New York Fed President Williams framed the yield surge as a reflection of economic strength rather than dysfunction, which helped equities snap a three-day losing streak. The scheduled path into the next 24 hours runs through the 12:30 UTC claims and trade block, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Services PMI, with August payrolls falling outside this window on Sep 4.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment de-escalated steadily. The Asian and European hours of Sep 2 carried Tail in the 20-23 band under an event/whipsaw then trend-down reading as the global long-end selloff pressed on index futures. From the 12:00 UTC hour onward Tail fell through the WATCH threshold to EA_ON as yields paused, Williams' remarks steadied sentiment and the cash session recovered, reaching a low of 11 in the late US evening before settling near 12 overnight. Five hourly slots have no published Claude assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are expected to stay range-like through the Asian and European sessions, with conditional risk concentrated in the 12:30-16:00 UTC block covering jobless claims, the US cash open and the ISM Services PMI. The mapped policy state is projected to move to WATCH for the 14:00 and 15:00 UTC hours on peak conditional Tail of 21, then decay back to EA_ON through the US afternoon. A modest late uptick is projected into the 19:00 UTC power hour on closing-auction and pre-payrolls positioning, after which conditions are projected to normalise into a compressed overnight band ahead of the Sep 4 payrolls report, which falls outside this window.
